latest_release.name: WM Keyboard 0.6.6
latest_release.body:
What's new in 0.6.6

 Plugins now run Python instead of Lua. One-row boards come in 36 languages, Avro included, and a smart punctuation key reads the sentence and offers its mark in 58 languages. Keys can take Expressive Keyboard's materials and Keys Cafe's press splashes, a photo can be cut up across the keys, Parakeet can run on the Snapdragon NPU, and WM Keyboard can be the phone's digital assistant and its voice input. ### Typing and autocorrect - Hold a word on the suggestion strip and pick **Correct to…** to teach autocorrect what it should become: type `kagay`, correct it to `lagay`, and the next `kagay` is fixed for you. - Number-row slips are fixed more readily when you type fast: two digits in a word ("y97" becomes "you") and a digit typed as a word's first letter ("5yped" becomes "typed"). Numbers such as "5pm", "4th" and "10am" stay as typed. - **Capitalize every word**, beside Automatic capital letters. - A smart punctuation key that reads the sentence and shows the mark it expects, in 58 languages, with a Standard and a Large model and a switch per language. - Choose which marks the automatic space follows. - A switch hides the underline under the word being typed. - Undo and redo backspace from the strip, the swipes that delete a whole line included, and a Retype button on the strip or the recent words' row ([#1189](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1189)). Two-thumb words get their own Backspace choice ([#1188](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1188)). - A long word borrows room from short ones on the strip, and next-word predictions fill the extra slots and the pages ([#1151](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1151), [#1154](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1154)). - Suggest characters by their Unicode name. - Swipe up or down on delete to delete whole lines ([#1162](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1162)). - Two-letter words get their accents back, and the last number-row and space-bar slips from [#1107](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1107) are fixed. - Glide: each language can have its own error radii ([#1136](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1136)), a word fixed the same way three times teaches the stroke, and learned shapes move to a checked binary file ([#1130](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1130)). - Pick several words to delete together from the personal dictionary ([#1134](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1134)). ### Languages and layouts - One-row boards in 36 languages, Avro among them, and a One-row QWERTY with the alphabet on a single row. They are a short strip in Minuum's manner: one key tall, the letters bare on the board at one size, each set a little higher or lower by its row on a full keyboard. - Unexpected Keyboard's QWERTY grid as an English layout. - Samsung's Indic boards show vowel signs after a consonant, with Samsung's page order. Gboard and Samsung layouts carry their own symbol pages. - Let it choose the word on eight more Indic languages. - Avro takes up a Bengali word under the caret with its suggestions, and a key over a selection spells a word. The word card's spelling bar types Avro Bangla and takes a paste ([#1190](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1190)). - Romanized dictation brings Banglish and Hinglish back in the spelling a reader expects. - Fancy Text gets 18 more styles, zalgo at the level you pick, and a strip you arrange. - Flick labels are sized and placed per key. A key in place of 🌐 can be any tool. - Ctrl+Shift alone can change the language on a hardware keyboard ([#1128](https://github.com/wasi-master/wmkeyboard/issues/1128)). - A removed language stops suggesting and takes its downloads with it. ### Themes and icons - Expressive Keyboard's looks: Soft, Pixel and Dot-matrix materials, Orbs and Meld effects, and Pop, Squish and Fade press motions. - Keys Cafe
